<p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">Indicate by check mark whether the registrant has submitted electronically every Interactive Data File required to be submitted pursuant to Rule 405 of Regulation S-T (&#167;232.405 of this chapter) during the preceding 12 months (or for such shorter period that the registrant was required to submit such files). <ix:nonNumeric name="dei:EntityInteractiveDataCurrent" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" id="ixv-15201">Yes</ix:nonNumeric> &#9746; No &#9744;</span></p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">Indicate by check mark whether the registrant is a large accelerated filer, an accelerated filer, a non-accelerated filer, a smaller reporting company or an emerging growth company. (See definitions of &#8220;large accelerated filer,&#8221; &#8220;accelerated filer,&#8221; &#8220;smaller reporting company&#8221; and &#8220;emerging growth company&#8221; in Rule 12b-2 of the Exchange Act).</span></p>
<p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>

Yes <ix:nonNumeric name="dei:EntityShellCompany" format="ixt-sec:boolballotbox" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" id="ixv-15205">&#9744;</ix:nonNumeric> No &#9746;</span></p>

Sky Harbour Group Corporation and its consolidated subsidiaries are collectively referred to as the &#8220;Company.&#8221;</span></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">The Company is organized as an umbrella partnership-C corporation, or &#8220;Up-C&#8221;, structure in which substantially all of the operating assets of the Company are held by Sky and SHG&#8217;s only substantive assets are its equity interests in Sky (the &#8220;Sky Common Units&#8221;). As of </span><span style="color:#000000;"><em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em></span><span style="color:#000000;">, SHG owned approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c145883127" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_OwnershipAxis-SkyHarbourLLCMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByParent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">44.9</ix:nonFraction>% of the Sky Common Units&#160;and the prior holders of Sky&#160;Common Units (the &#8220;LLC Interests&#8221;) owned approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c145883128" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_LegalEntityAxis-LLCInterestsAndTRAHoldersMember_OwnershipAxis-SkyHarbourLLCMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByParent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">55.1</ix:nonFraction>% of the Sky Common Units and control the Company through their ownership of the Company's Class B Common Stock, $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883129" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_LegalEntityAxis-SkyHarbourLLCMember_StatementClassOfStockAxis-CommonClassBMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.0001</ix:nonFraction> par value (&#8220;Class B Common Stock&#8221;).</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">&#160;</span></p>
  </ix:nonNumeric>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><b><i>Basis of Presentation</i></b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">The accompanying unaudited consolidated financial statements and the related notes (the &#8220;Financial Statements&#8221;) have been prepared in conformity with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;) requirements for quarterly reports on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Q, and consequently exclude certain disclosures normally included in audited consolidated financial statements prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;). These Financial Statements include the accounts of SHG&#160;and its consolidated subsidiaries. All intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation. The Financial Statements should be read in conjunction with the audited consolidated financial statements and the notes contained in the Company&#8217;s Annual Report on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>which includes additional disclosures and a summary of the Company's significant accounting policies. In the Company&#8217;s opinion, these Financial Statements include all adjustments, consisting of normal recurring items, considered necessary by management to fairly state the Company&#8217;s results of operation, financial position, and cash flows.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">Certain historical amounts have been reclassified to conform to the current year&#8217;s presentation.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><b><i>Use of Estimates </i></b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">The preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires the Company to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting periods. Such estimates include assumptions used within impairment analyses, estimated useful lives of depreciable assets and amortizable costs, estimates of inputs utilized in determining the fair value of financial instruments such as warrants, and estimates and assumptions related to right-of-use assets and operating lease liabilities. Actual results could differ materially from those estimates.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><b><i>Risks and Uncertainties</i></b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">The Company is subject to risks and uncertainties common to early-stage companies. For most of its history, the Company has been&#160;engaged in securing access to land through ground leases and developing and constructing aviation hangars. The major risks faced by the Company are its future ability to obtain additional tenants for the facilities that it constructs, and to contract with such tenants for rental income in an amount that is sufficient to meet the Company&#8217;s financial obligations, including increasing construction costs due to inflation and increased borrowing costs to the extent that the Company incurs additional indebtedness.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><b><i>Liquidity and Capital Resources</i></b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">As a result of ongoing construction projects and business development activities, including the development of aircraft hangars and the leasing of available hangar space, the Company has incurred recurring losses and negative cash flows from operating activities since its inception. The Company expects to continue to invest in such activities and generate operating losses in the near future.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">The Company obtained long-term financing through bond and equity offerings, committed bank drawdown facility, and has the ability to&#160;utilize its at-the-market&#160;offering program&#160;to fund its construction, lease, and operational commitments, and believes its liquidity is sufficient to allow continued operations for more than <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year after the date these financial statements are issued.</span></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><b><i>Significant Accounting Policies</i></b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><i>Basis of Consolidation</i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">SHG is deemed to have a controlling interest of Sky through its appointment as the managing member of Sky, in which SHG has control over the affairs and decision-making of Sky. The interests in Sky <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> owned by the Company are presented as non-controlling interests. Sky&#8217;s ownership percentage in each of its consolidated subsidiaries is <ix:nonFraction id="c145883136" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_LegalEntityAxis-SkyHarbourLLCMember_OwnershipAxis-ConsolidatedSubsidiariesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByParent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>%, unless otherwise disclosed.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><i>Cost of Construction </i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">Cost of construction on the accompanying consolidated balance sheets is carried at cost. The cost of acquiring an asset includes the costs necessary to bring a capital project to the condition necessary for its intended use. Costs are capitalized once the construction of a specific capital project is probable. Construction labor and other direct costs of construction are capitalized. Professional fees for engineering, procurement, consulting, and other soft costs that are directly identifiable with the project and are considered an incremental direct cost are capitalized. Activities associated with internally manufactured&#160;hangar buildings, including materials, direct manufacturing labor, and manufacturing overhead directly identifiable with such activities are allocated to our construction projects and capitalized. The Company allocates a portion of its internal salaries to both capitalized cost of construction and to general and administrative expense based on the percentage of time certain employees worked in the related areas. Interest, net of the amortization of debt issuance costs and premiums, and net of interest income earned on bond proceeds, is also capitalized until the capital projects are&#160;completed.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">Once a capital project is complete, the Company begins to depreciate the constructed asset on a straight-line basis over the lesser of the estimated useful life of the asset or the remaining term of the related ground lease, including expected renewal terms.&#160;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><i>Leases</i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">The Company accounts for leases under Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) Topic <em style="font: inherit;">842,</em> Leases. The Company determines whether a contract contains a lease at the inception of the contract. ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">842</em> requires lessees to recognize lease liabilities and right-of-use (&#8220;ROU&#8221;) assets for all operating leases with terms of more than <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months on the consolidated balance sheets. The Company has made an accounting policy election to <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognize leases with an initial term of <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months or less on the&#160;Company&#8217;s consolidated balance sheets and will recognize&#160;those lease payments in the consolidated statements of operations on a straight-line basis over the lease term. When management determines that it is reasonably certain that the Company will exercise its options to renew the leases, the renewal terms are included in the lease term and the resulting ROU asset and lease liability balances.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">The Company has lease agreements with lease and non-lease components; the Company has elected the accounting policy to <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> separate lease and non-lease components for all underlying asset classes. The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> elected to capitalize any interest cost that is implicit within its operating leases into cost of construction on the consolidated balance sheet, but instead, expenses its ground lease cost as a component of operating expenses&#160;in the consolidated statements of operations.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">All of the Company&#8217;s ground leases at airports are classified as operating leases under ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">842.</em> Management has determined that it is reasonably certain that the Company will exercise its options to renew the leases, and therefore the renewal options are included in the lease term and the resulting ROU asset and operating lease liability balances. As the Company&#8217;s lease agreements do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> provide a readily determinable implicit rate, nor is the rate available to the Company from its lessors, the Company uses its incremental borrowing rate to determine the present value of the lease payments.</span></p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">The Company has operating leases that contain variable payments, most commonly in the form of common area maintenance and operating expense charges, which are based on actual costs incurred. These variable payments were excluded from the calculation of the ROU asset and operating lease liability balances since they are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> fixed or in-substance fixed payments. These variable payments were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> material in amount for&#160;the </span><span style="color:#000000;"><em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em></span><span style="color:#000000;">. Some of the leases contain covenants that require the Company to construct the hangar facilities on the leased grounds within a certain period and spend a set minimum dollar amount. For <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of the leases, the shortfall (if any) must be paid to the lessor. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">18</em>&#160;&#8212;&#160;<i>Commitments and Contingencies</i>.</span></p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><i>Warrants liability</i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">The Company accounts for its Warrants&#160;(as defined in Note <em style="font: inherit;">11</em>&#160;&#8212;&#160;<i>Warrants</i>) in accordance with the guidance contained in ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815,</em> &#8220;Derivatives and Hedging&#8221; (&#8220;ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815&#8221;</em>), under which warrants that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the criteria for equity classification and must be recorded as derivative liabilities. Accordingly, the Company classifies the Warrants as liabilities carried at their fair value and adjusts the warrants to fair value at each reporting period. This liability is subject to re-measurement at each balance sheet date until the warrants are exercised or expire, and any change in fair value is recognized in the consolidated statement of operations.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><i>Revenue recognition </i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">The Company leases the hangar facilities that it constructs to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>&#160;parties.&#160;The Company determines whether a contract contains a lease at the inception of the contract. The lease agreements are either on a month-to-month basis or have a defined term and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>have options to extend the term. Some of the leases contain options to terminate the lease by either party with given notice. The Company expects to continue to derive benefit from the underlying assets after the end of the lease term through further leasing arrangements. The underlying assets are the leasehold interest that the Company has in connection with its ground leases. There are&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;options given to the lessee to purchase the underlying assets.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">Rental revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">842</em>&#160;and includes fixed payments of cash rents, which represents revenue each tenant pays in accordance with the terms of its respective lease and is recognized on a straight-line basis over the term of the lease. Rental revenue and the corresponding rent and other receivables are recorded net of any concessions and uncollectible tenant receivables, if any, for all periods presented. The Company evaluates the collectability of tenant receivables for payments required under the lease agreements. If the Company determines that collectability is&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;probable, the Company recognizes any difference between revenue amounts recognized to date under ASC&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">842</em>&#160;and payments that have been collected from the lessee, including any additional rent or lease termination fees, as a current period adjustment to rental revenue.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">At certain of the Company&#8217;s hangar campuses, the Company recognizes revenue from ground-based services, such as the fueling and towing of aircraft under ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> Revenue from Contracts with Customers. Revenue for the sale of&#160;aircraft fuel&#160;is recognized at the time customer obtains control of the fuel. Revenue for the sale of other ground-based services is recognized at the time&#160;the service is performed and provided to customers. Customers are invoiced at the time the services are performed and the associated revenue is recognized in the period it is earned. The Company&#8217;s fueling arrangements generally are unique at each location it operates, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be accounted for on a gross or net basis. The Company determines whether to recognize fuel and services revenue on a gross or net basis based on consideration of various factors, including whether the Company has control of the products or services prior to delivery to customers, the Company&#8217;s degree of latitude in establishing the sales price, whether the Company carries the associated inventory risk, and which party is the primary obligor within such sales arrangements.&#160;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">For the </span><span style="color:#000000;"><em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em></span><span style="color:#000000;">&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> the Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145883165"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145884326">not</span></span> derive <em style="font: inherit;">10%</em> of its revenue from any single tenant.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><i>Income Taxes</i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">SHG is classified as a corporation for U.S. Federal income tax purposes and is subject to U.S. Federal and state income taxes. SHG includes in income, for U.S. Federal income tax purposes, its allocable portion of income from the &#8220;pass-through&#8221; entities in which it holds an interest, including Sky. The &#8220;pass-through&#8221; entities&#160;are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to U.S. Federal and certain state income taxes at the entity level, and instead, the tax liabilities with respect to taxable income are passed through to the members, including SHG. As a result, prior to the transactions contemplated by that certain Equity Purchase Agreement, dated as of <em style="font: inherit;"> August 1, 2021, </em>by and among Yellowstone Acquisition Company (&#8220;YAC&#8221;) and Sky, which we refer to as the&#160;Yellowstone Transaction, Sky was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to U.S. Federal and certain state income taxes at the entity level.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">The Company follows the asset and liability method of accounting for income taxes. This method gives consideration to the future tax consequences associated with the differences between the financial accounting and tax basis of the assets and liabilities as well as the ultimate realization of any deferred tax asset resulting from such differences, as well as from net operating losses and other tax-basis carryforwards. Valuation allowances are recorded to reduce deferred tax assets when it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that a tax benefit will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized. When a valuation allowance is increased or decreased, a corresponding tax expense or benefit is recorded.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">The Company recorded income tax expense of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883171" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction> and the effective tax rate was <ix:nonFraction id="c145883172" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0.0</ix:nonFraction>% for the </span><span style="color:#000000;"><em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em></span><span style="color:#000000;">&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em> The effective income tax rate for the&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;"><em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em></span><span style="color:#000000;">&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> differs from the federal statutory rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c145883177" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-SalesRevenueNetMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">21</ix:nonFraction>% primarily due to a full valuation allowance against net deferred tax assets as it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the deferred tax assets will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized due to the cumulative losses sustained by the Company to date.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><i><b>Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements</b></i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024,&#160;</em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">No.</em>&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em><i>,</i>&#160;<i>Income Statement</i>&#160;&#8212;<i> Reporting Comprehensive Income: Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic</i>&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</i>. This ASU requires public business entities to disclose in the notes to financial statements specific categories within relevant expense captions presented on the face of the income statement. The ASU is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026,&#160;</em>and interim reporting periods beginning after&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027.&#160;</em>Early adoption is permitted. The amendments should be applied on a prospective basis with retrospective application permitted. We are currently evaluating the impact of adopting this ASU on our consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</span></p>

   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 0pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> </b></span></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><b>Investments and Restricted Investments</b></span></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">Investments of the Company&#8217;s cash in various U.S. Treasury securities that have been classified as available-for-sale and are carried at estimated fair value utilizing Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> inputs as&#160;determined based upon quoted market prices. Investments of the&#160;funds held in the restricted trust bank accounts associated with the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Bonds and the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds, as defined in Note <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> &#8212;&#160;<i>Bonds payable, loans payable, and interest</i>, are reported as &#8220;Restricted investments&#8221; in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets. Such investments are classified as available-for-sale or held-to-maturity at the time of investment.&#160;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">Unrealized losses on certain of the Company&#8217;s investments and restricted investments are primarily attributable to changes in interest rates. The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> believe the unrealized losses represent impairments because the unrealized losses are due to general market factors. The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognized an allowance for expected credit losses related to its investments or restricted investments as the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> identified any unrealized losses attributable to credit factors during the </span><span style="color:#000000;"><em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em></span><span style="color:#000000;">. The held-to-maturity restricted investments are carried on the consolidated balance sheet at amortized cost. As of </span><span style="color:#000000;"><em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em></span><span style="color:#000000;">, the Company has the ability and intent to hold these restricted investments until maturity, and as a result, the Company would <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect the value of these investments to decline significantly due to a sudden change in market interest rates. The fair value of the Company&#8217;s restricted investments is estimated utilizing Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> inputs including prices for U.S. Treasury securities with comparable maturities on active markets.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>

     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000"><i>Tax-Exempt Series</i>&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">2026</em></i>&#160;<i>Bonds</i>&#160;<i>Issuance</i></span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 12, 2026,&#160;</em>Sky Harbour Capital III LLC (&#8220;Sky Capital III&#8221;), an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, completed a $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883250" contextRef="d_2026-02-12_2026-02-12_DebtInstrumentAxis-Series2026BondsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfDebt" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">150</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million financing through the issuance of Revenue Bonds (Sky Harbour Capital III LLC Aviation Facilities Project), Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;(the &#8220;Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bonds&#8221;). The Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bonds were issued by the Public Finance Authority of Wisconsin, a multi-jurisdictional conduit issuer (the &#8220;Issuer&#8221;), pursuant to a Trust Indenture, dated as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2026 (</em>the &#8220;Indenture&#8221;) and effective as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 12, 2026,&#160;</em>between the Issuer and UMB Bank, N.A., as trustee (the &#8220;Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bond Trustee&#8221;). The proceeds of the Bonds were used to make a loan (the &#8220;Loan&#8221;) to Sky Capital III pursuant to a Loan Agreement, dated as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 1, 2026 (</em>the &#8220;Loan Agreement&#8221;), between the Issuer and Sky Capital III, and assigned to the Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bond Trustee. The Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bonds were issued in a limited offering (the &#8220;Offering&#8221;) pursuant to a Limited Offering Memorandum dated&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 29, 2026 (</em>the &#8220;Limited Offering Memorandum&#8221;) to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">144A</em>&#160;under the Securities Act of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">1933,</em>&#160;as amended (the &#8220;Securities Act&#8221;) or accredited investors within the meaning of Rule&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">501</em>(a) under the Securities Act. The borrowings under the Loan Agreement are guaranteed (the &#8220;Guarantee&#8221;) by Sky, and Sky Harbour Holdings IV LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Sky (the &#8220;Pledgor&#8221;). Pursuant to the Indenture, all of the Issuer&#8217;s right, title, and interest in the Loan Agreement (except for certain unassigned rights) were assigned to the Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bond Trustee. The Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bonds are secured by the Loan Agreement and the residual cash flows of certain of the Company&#8217;s projects, and payment of the Bonds is structurally subordinate to the Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;Bonds and borrowings under the Term Loan Facility.</span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">The Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bonds and borrowings under the Loan Agreement bear interest at a rate of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145883264" contextRef="i_2026-02-12_DebtInstrumentAxis-Series2026BondsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">6.00</ix:nonFraction>% per year, payable semi-annually in arrears on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 1&#160;</em>and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> July 1&#160;</em>of each year, beginning on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2026.&#160;</em>The Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bonds are subject to mandatory tender for purchase on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2031 (</em>the &#8220;Mandatory Tender Date&#8221;), and will mature on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2060,&#160;</em>unless earlier exchanged, redeemed or repurchased. On the Mandatory Tender Date, holders will be required to tender their Bonds for purchase at a price equal to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145883266" contextRef="d_2026-02-12_2026-02-12_DebtInstrumentAxis-Series2026BondsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentRedemptionPricePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the principal amount thereof plus accrued interest. Following such mandatory tender, the Bonds&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be remarketed at a new interest rate or otherwise refinanced. Accordingly, although the Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bonds have a stated final maturity of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2060,&#160;</em>Sky Capital III will be required to refinance or remarket the Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bonds on or prior to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2031.</em></span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">The principal amount of the Loan is $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883269" contextRef="i_2026-02-12_DebtInstrumentAxis-Series2026BondsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">150</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. The Company intends to use the proceeds from the Loan, together with other available funds, including draws from the Company&#8217;s Term Loan Facility, to (i) finance or refinance, directly or indirectly, all or a portion of the construction, equipping and/or improvement of all or a portion of certain aircraft storage facilities (collectively, the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2026</em>&#160;Projects&#8221;); (ii) fund a deposit to the debt service reserve fund for the Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bonds; (iii) pay capitalized interest on the Loan through&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2029;&#160;</em>and (iv) pay the costs of issuance of the Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bonds.</span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">The Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bonds are subject to (a) optional redemption at the discretion of Sky Capital III at any time on or after&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2030&#160;</em>at a redemption price equal to the principal amount plus a&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">1%</em>&#160;premium and accrued and unpaid interest to the redemption date, (b) mandatory redemption upon the occurrence of a determination of taxability of the Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Bonds, and (c) mandatory sinking fund redemption beginning in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2056.</em></span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">Sky Capital III expects to meet its payment obligations under the Loan Agreement from funds to the extent available and permitted to be released under the master trust indenture with respect to the Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;Bonds and the Term Loan Facility. Interest is capitalized through&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2029.</em></span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">The Indenture and the Loan Agreement provide for customary events of default, all as described in the Indenture and the Loan Agreement.</span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 9pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 11px; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000"><i>Term Loan Facility Amendments</i></span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 8, 2026, </em>Sky Harbour Capital II LLC (&#8220;SH Capital II&#8221;), an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, entered into an amendment (the &#8220;Amendment&#8221;) to the Term Loan Facility. The Amendment amended the Term Loan Facility to&#160;provide&#160;for, among other things, conditions under which surplus funds, as defined in the Amendment (the&#160;&#8220;Term Loan Facility Surplus Funds&#8221;),&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be released to SH Capital II and its special purpose subsidiaries (the&#160;&#8220;Term Loan&#160;Borrowers&#8221;).&#160;Also on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 8, 2026,&#160;</em>subsidiaries of the Company that own existing and future hangar campuses at CMA and BDL were added to the borrowing base of the Term Loan Facility. Subsequently, on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 8, 2026,&#160;</em>SH Capital II drew funds of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883278" contextRef="d_2026-01-08_2026-01-08_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfDebt" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">13</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million under the Term Loan Facility in order to reimburse the Company for prior advances associated with capital expenditures at Bradley International Airport and certain other general corporate purposes.&#160;</span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">In addition, Sky Harbour Holdings III LLC (&#8220;SKYH III&#8221;) amended its related guaranty (the&#160;&#8220;Sky&#160;III Guaranty&#8221;, and such amendment, the &#8220;Sky III Guaranty Amendment&#8221;) to provide for, among other things, conditions under which surplus funds arising from&#160;amounts received by Sky from excess revenues released from the Master Indenture <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be utilized by Sky, as discussed below.&#160;</span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">Provided certain conditions within the Amendment are met, the Amendment permits the Term Loan Borrowers to distribute or otherwise transfer such Term Loan Facility Surplus Funds to (i) Sky (the &#8220;Parent Guarantor&#8221;) for the payment of general and administrative expenses of the Parent Guarantor, (ii) the payment of current interest or principal on indebtedness of the Parent Guarantor or indebtedness guaranteed by the Parent Guarantor, (iii) to deposit or transfer such funds into a separate account of an affiliate of the Parent Guarantor as security for the payment of principal&#160;of or interest on other&#160;indebtedness, or (iv) as a capital contribution of a Term Loan Borrower&#160;for the approved construction and operation of hangar project facilities at various airports (the &#8220;Portfolio II&#160;Projects&#8221;, and such restriction on distributions and transfers the &#8220;Permissible Uses&#8221;). The Amendment&#160;permits the release of the Term Loan Facility Surplus Funds beginning on the later&#160;of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2027&#160;</em>or a trigger date based on substantial completion of certain Portfolio II Projects, and requires the Term Loan Borrowers to maintain (i) a&#160;historical debt service coverage ratio, and a&#160;(ii) projected debt service coverage ratio, in each case determined on the last day of each fiscal quarter of the Term Loan Borrowers, at a ratio of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;less than&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2.00</em>&#160;to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">1.00.</em></span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">The Sky III Guaranty Amendment permits the release of excess revenues released from the Master Trust on or after the later of (i)&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2027&#160;</em>and (ii)&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;(<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) months after the Capitalized Interest End Date provided that (a) there are funds in excess of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883284" contextRef="i_2026-01-08_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentReleaseOfExcessRevenueFundsOnDepositsInAccountsBenchmark" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">800,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;on deposit in the accounts for such excess revenues on release date, and (b) to the extent there is a deficiency in any of the accounts associated with the Term Loan Facility, there are sufficient funds on deposit (in addition to the minimum amount of funds held pursuant to cover such &#160;deficiency) and such funds are applied to remedy each such deficiency. The release of excess revenues is also subject to Permissible Uses.</span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">The above release conditions are also subject to the customary condition that there&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;be any default under the Term Loan Facility.</span>
     </div>
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
       &#160;
     </div>
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>there was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883286" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentUnusedBorrowingCapacityAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">180.6</ix:nonFraction> million of availability under the Term Loan Facility, subject to borrowing base restrictions.</span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 9pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 11px; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000"><i><em style="font: inherit;">2026</em></i>&#160;<i>Yorkville Promissory Note</i></span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 27, 2026,&#160;</em>Sky issued a non-convertible, unsecured promissory note to YA II PN, Ltd., a Cayman Islands exempt limited company, or its registered assigns (&#8220;Yorkville&#8221;), in the aggregate principal amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883288" contextRef="i_2026-01-27_DebtInstrumentAxis-January2026YorkvillePromissoryNoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">10</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million (the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> &#8220;January 2026&#160;</em>Yorkville Promissory Note&#8221;). The issue price for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026&#160;</em>Yorkville Promissory Note was&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145883289" contextRef="i_2026-01-27_DebtInstrumentAxis-January2026YorkvillePromissoryNoteMember" unitRef="Pure" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentIssuancePricePercentageOfAggregatePrincipalAmount" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the aggregate principal amount thereof.</span>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <p style="text-indent: 18pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
     <div style="font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
      <span style="color:#000000">The&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026&#160;</em>Yorkville Promissory Note accrues interest at a rate of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145883290" contextRef="i_2026-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-January2026YorkvillePromissoryNoteMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">7.75</ix:nonFraction>% per annum (or&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145883291" contextRef="i_2026-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-January2026YorkvillePromissoryNoteMember" unitRef="Pure" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentDefaultInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">18</ix:nonFraction>% upon the occurrence of an event of default) and matures on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 8, 2027.&#160;</em>Beginning on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> July 8, 2026,&#160;</em>and continuing on the same day of each of the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em>&#160;successive months thereafter, Sky shall repay a portion of the outstanding balance of the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026&#160;</em>Yorkville Promissory Note in an amount equal to $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883293" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-January2026YorkvillePromissoryNoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentPeriodicPayment" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">833,333.33</ix:nonFraction>. The obligations of Sky&#160;under the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026&#160;</em>Yorkville Promissory Note are guaranteed by the Company pursuant to a separate guaranty agreement between the Company and Yorkville. In connection with and pursuant to the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026&#160;</em>Yorkville Promissory Note, the Company issued <ix:nonFraction id="c145883294" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-January2026YorkvillePromissoryNoteMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">40,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of Class A Common Stock&#160;to Yorkville. The&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026&#160;</em>Yorkville Promissory Note contains customary representations and warranties by Sky&#160;and the Company and customary events of default. The proceeds of the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026&#160;</em>Yorkville Promissory Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be used for working capital and general corporate purposes.</span>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">SHG&#8217;s legal predecessor, YAC,&#160;issued&#160;to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party investors&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145883298" contextRef="i_2020-10-26_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PublicWarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">6,799,439</ix:nonFraction>&#160;warrants which entitled the holder to purchase&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;share of Class A Common Stock at an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883300" contextRef="i_2020-10-26_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PublicWarrantsMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11.50</ix:nonFraction>&#160;per share (the &#8220;Public Warrants&#8221;). In addition,&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145883301" contextRef="i_2020-10-26_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">7,719,779</ix:nonFraction>&#160;private placement warrants were sold to BOC Yellowstone LLC&#160;(the &#8220;Sponsor&#8221;). Each Private Warrant allows the Sponsor to purchase&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;share of Class A Common Stock at an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883303" contextRef="i_2020-10-26_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11.50</ix:nonFraction>&#160;per share. The Public Warrants and Private Warrants remain outstanding under the same terms and conditions to purchase shares of the Company&#8217;s Class A Common Stock. The terms of the Private Warrants are identical to those of the Public Warrants, except for that so long as the Private Warrants are held by the Sponsor or its permitted transferees, they&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be exercised on a cashless basis.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">In connection with the&#160;Securities Purchase Agreement (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2023</em> Purchase Agreement&#8221;) entered into on <em style="font: inherit;"> November 1, 2023 </em>with certain investors, the Company issued to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party investors&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145883306" contextRef="i_2023-11-01_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,541,600</ix:nonFraction> warrants (the &#8220;PIPE Warrants&#8221;, and together with the Public Warrants and the Private Warrants, the &#8220;Warrants&#8221;). The PIPE Warrants are equivalent in form and substance to the Company&#8217;s Public Warrants.&#160;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">The Warrants contain an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883307" contextRef="i_2023-11-01_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11.50</ix:nonFraction>&#160;per share and expire on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 25, 2027.&#160;</em>The Company determined the fair value of its Public Warrants and PIPE Warrants based on the publicly listed trading price as of the valuation date. Accordingly, these warrants are classified as Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>&#160;financial instruments. As the terms of the Private Warrants are identical to those of the Public Warrants, the Company determined the fair value of its Private Warrants based on the publicly listed trading price of the Public Warrants as of the valuation date and have classified the Private Warrants as Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>&#160;financial instruments.</span></p>

With respect to stock dividends, holders of Class A Common Stock must receive Class A Common Stock. The holders of Class B Common Stock do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have any right to receive dividends other than stock dividends consisting of shares of Class B Common Stock, as applicable, in each case paid proportionally with respect to each outstanding share of Class B Common Stock.</span></p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">Basic earnings (loss) per share of Class A Common Stock is computed by dividing net income (loss) attributable to SHG by the weighted-average number of shares of Class A Common Stock outstanding during the period. Diluted net income (loss) per share of Class A Common Stock is computed by dividing net income (loss) attributable to SHG, adjusted for the assumed exchange of all potentially dilutive securities, by the weighted-average number of shares of Class A Common Stock outstanding adjusted to give effect to potentially dilutive shares using the treasury stock or if-converted method as appropriate. Shares of the Company&#8217;s Class B Common Stock do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> participate in the earnings or losses of the Company and are therefore <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> participating securities. As such, separate presentation of basic and diluted earnings per share of Class B Common Stock under the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-class method has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been presented.&#160;</span></p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">The Company has&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145883374">one</span>&#160;consolidated reportable segment. This segment derives revenues from customers through the leasing of home-basing aircraft hangars and through services and products ancillary to its leasing activities. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>the Company drives revenue entirely within the United States&#160;and manages the business activities on a consolidated basis.</span></p>
   <div style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">
    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">The determination of reportable operating segments is based on the Chief Operating Decision Maker&#8217;s (&#8220;CODM&#8217;s&#8221;) use of financial information provided for the purposes of assessing performance and making operating decisions. The Company&#8217;s CODM is its founder and Chief Executive Officer. The CODM uses net income (loss) to allocate resources and assess the performance of the Company by comparing actual results to historical results and previously forecasted financial information and the allocation of budget between the expenses presented within the consolidated statement of operations. The measure of segment assets is reported on the consolidated balance sheet as total consolidated assets. All required significant financial segment information can be found within the consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;</span></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><i>Loan and Security Agreement</i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 6, 2024,&#160;</em>the Company entered into a revolving line of credit loan and security agreement&#160;(the &#8220;Loan and Security Agreement&#8221;), with a company controlled by the former owner of the Company&#8217;s acquired subsidiaries at Camarillo Airport (&#8220;CMA&#8221;),&#160;who also serves as&#160;an independent contractor of the Company. The Company provided an initial loan commitment of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883380" contextRef="i_2024-12-06_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-IndependentContractorMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:NotesReceivableGross" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and agreed to provide an additional $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883381" contextRef="i_2024-12-06_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-IndependentContractorMember" unitRef="USD" name="skyh:LoansReceivableAdditionalWorkingCapitalLoanAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">2.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of availability under a revolving line of credit to fund the working capital requirements of such company. The Loan and Security Agreement matures on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 6, 2029,&#160;</em>and bears interest at&#160;the&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145884403">standard overnight financing&#160;right</span> plus&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145883382" contextRef="i_2024-12-06_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-IndependentContractorMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:LoansReceivableBasisSpreadOnVariableRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">2</ix:nonFraction>% per annum.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">As of </span><span style="color:#000000;"><em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em></span><span style="color:#000000;"> and&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;"><em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em></span><span style="color:#000000;">,&#160;the Company had loaned a total of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883383" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-IndependentContractorMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:NotesReceivableGross" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145883384" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-IndependentContractorMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:NotesReceivableGross" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively,&#160;to such company, the balance of which is presented as a component of accounts receivable, prepaid expenses, and other assets within the Company&#8217;s consolidated balance sheet.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;"><i>Echo Echo Agreement</i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 19, 2024,&#160;</em>the Company entered into an additional non-exclusive agreement with Echo Echo, LLC for the use of an Epic&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">E1000GX</em>&#160;aircraft. The effective date of the agreement was&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> August 30, 2024&#160;</em>and the agreement automatically renews annually.&#160;The agreement can be terminated without penalty if either party provides&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">30</em>&#160;days&#8217; written notice, or if the aircraft is sold or otherwise disposed of. Additionally, the Company is responsible for reimbursing its&#160;pro rata share of the direct operating costs of the aircraft, exclusive of maintenance and insurance.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>

The related liability is included in Accounts payable, accrued expenses and other liabilities within&#160;the consolidated balance sheet as of </span><span style="color:#000000;"><em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em></span><span style="color:#000000;">.</span></p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><span style="color:#000000;"><b>Overview and Background</b></span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: -9pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 9pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">We are an aviation infrastructure development company building the first nationwide network of Home Base Operator (&#8220;HBO&#8221;)&#160;campuses designed exclusively for business aircraft. We develop, lease and manage general aviation hangars across the United States, targeting airfields in markets with significant based aircraft populations and high hangar demand. Our HBO&#160;campuses feature private and semi-private hangars and a full suite of dedicated services specifically optimized&#160;for home based, versus transient, aircraft.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">The&#160;physical footprint of the U.S. business aviation fleet grew by almost 46 million&#160;square feet in the past sixteen years, with hangar supply lagging dramatically, especially in key growth markets. As the fleet of private jets in the United States continues to grow, with recent new aircraft deliveries exceeding retirements, demand for hangar space is at a premium in part because new jets require taller tail clearances and more square footage of hangar space&#160;and the pace of new hangar construction has lagged behind the demand. The cumulative square footage of the business aircraft fleet in the United States increased 73% between 2010 and 2025. Moreover, over that same period, there was an 120% increase in the square footage of larger private jets &#8211; those with greater than a 24-foot tail height. A recent study conducted by a business aircraft manufacturer&#160;forecasted&#160;that business aircraft will only continue to grow in the next ten years, with up to 8,500 new business jet deliveries worth over&#160;$283 billion expected to be delivered between 2025 and 2034, with over two-thirds of the deliveries expected to be comprised of larger private jets. This forecast is further supported by data from the major business aviation manufacturers that suggest the current&#160;order backlog for new business aviation aircraft as of December 31, 2025 is over $57 billion, an increase of approximately 10% over the prior year.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">These larger footprint aircraft do not fit in much of the existing hangar infrastructure and impose stacking challenges and constraints in the traditional shared or community hangars operated by fixed-base operators (&#8220;FBO&#8221;). The addition of winglets (the vertical extensions on aircraft wingtips) on most modern business jets inhibits wing-over-wing storage. Aircraft hangars are in high demand and short supply, with some airports compiling waiting lists that can exceed several years.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <div class="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
   <div class="PGFTR" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">
    <div class="hf-row">
     <div class="hf-cell PGNUM" style="text-align: center; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman;">
      23

    <div class="hf-row">
     <div class="hf-cell TOCLink" style="display: inline-block; text-align: left;">
      <a href="#toc" style="font-weight: initial; font-style: initial; font-variant: initial; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Table of Contents</a>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 9pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">We believe our scalable, real estate-centric business model is uniquely positioned to capture this market opportunity and address the increased imbalance between the supply and demand for private jet storage. We intend to capitalize on the existing hangar supply constraints at major U.S. airports by targeting high-end tenants in markets where there is a shortage of private and FBO hangar space, or where such hangars are or are becoming obsolete.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">We expect to realize economies of scale in construction through prototype hangar designs replicated at our HBO campuses across the United States through our in-house construction management and general contracting. This allows for centralized procurement, straightforward permitting processes, efficient development processes, and the best hangar in business aviation. Unlike a service company, our revenues are mostly derived&#160;from long-term rental agreements, offering stability and forward visibility of revenues and cash flows. This allows us to fund our development through the public bond market and bank debt, providing capital efficiency and mitigating refinance risk.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="color:#000000;">We seek to develop our home basing&#160;hangar campuses on long-term ground leases (or sub-leases thereof) at airports with suitable infrastructure serving metropolitan centers across the United States.&#160;We lease each of our properties under long-term ground leases.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
